If you post a new submission to a subverse, it's stuck at the bottom of the subverse's Hot feed (which in many cases means it doesn't show up there at all unless you go deeper in the feed), until someone who sees it in New upvoats it. Then it takes precedence over the old posts. The algorithm works similarly with comments, as far as I can tell.

I think this is wrong and should be fixed. Of course, a very popular day-old post should still take precedence over new posts, but new and unupvoated submissions should take precedence over old, moderately upvoated submissions in the Hot feed. New submissions are why you come back to a subverse, after all.

What do you think?
Fix the sorting/ranking algorithm to put new submissions higher up in the Hot feed

IMO the best option would be if there were a setting on how fast posts "rot". Users not on voat for a week should see the most interesting of the week, users refreshing for the 9001st time should get the posts of the last few minutes.

But that would put a lot more load on the database, so it's not the right time for it now.
Constantly refreshing users are going to go to the New feed anyway. IMO there's no need to cater to them in the Hot feed.

A valid point. It was meant as an extreme, the idea is to show an user the most interesting stuff in a certain timespan. The timespan might be weeks or minutes. IMO the front page should not be covered with old news or be filled with /v/all/new, but the timespan of interesting posts is different for everyone.

See this: https://voat.co/v/voatdev/comments/145217

My guess is that, since it is never initialized, the rank of a post is essentially random to start. Sometimes it will go to the top, sometimes it will get a low rank and go to the bottom. Upvoating or downvoating the post should give it an accurate rank

Also the first X votes need to be hidden and not contribute the score for a period of time. On Reddit the first downvote always had such a huge impact on whether it hits the first page of the subreddit or not. It encouraged people who posted to scope out the "new" page and downvote all other posts.
